title: Alljoined-1.6M
description: Alljoined-1.6M is a large-scale EEG dataset capturing neural responses of 20 healthy adults to rapid serial visual presentation of natural images from the THINGS database, recorded using a consumer-grade 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system across four sessions per participant. With over 1.6 million stimulus trials, the dataset aims to assess whether affordable EEG hardware can support deep learning-based brain-computer interface and semantic decoding research comparable to expensive research-grade systems. Its design mirrors the THINGS-EEG2 stimulus set to facilitate direct cross-dataset comparisons.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system (sintered Ag/AgCl gel electrodes, wireless Bluetooth 5.2) at 256 Hz, using an extended 10-20 montage focused on occipital/visual regions, with built-in dual 50/60 Hz notch filtering. Participants viewed images for 100 ms followed by 100 ms blank in an RSVP oddball paradigm, performing button-press detection of Woody character catch trials. Raw data were exported as EDF files, and converted to BIDS format using MNE-BIDS with channel renaming and metadata channel exclusion.
